hints: Focus on the clue that no gas was produced, so think about which reagents normally release a gas with a carboxylic acid.
Remember that both carbonates and hydrogencarbonates react with acids to give off carbon dioxide gas.
Think about which reagent gives only the sodium salt plus water, with no gaseous product to complete the choice.
walkthrough:
**Identify what propanoic acid can do**

Propanoic acid is a typical weak carboxylic acid. It will neutralise bases, alkalis, carbonates and hydrogencarbonates to form the propanoate salt.

General idea:
$$\text{acid} + \text{base} \rightarrow \text{salt} + \text{water (no gas)}$$
$$\text{acid} + \text{carbonate} \rightarrow \text{salt} + \text{water} + \text{CO}_2 \text{(gas)}$$

**Check the gas-producing options**

Both $\text{NaHCO}_3$ and $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ contain carbonate. They react like this and bubble $\text{CO}_2$:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} + \text{NaHCO}_3 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COONa} + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2$$
Since the question says no gas was produced, these two cannot be correct.

**Find the no-gas neutralisation**

Sodium hydroxide is an alkali. It simply neutralises the acid to give the salt and water only:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COONa} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
This matches both observations, sodium propanoate formed and no gas evolved.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{NaHCO}_3$ is a hydrogencarbonate and reacts with propanoic acid to give sodium propanoate plus water and carbon dioxide gas, so gas would be seen.
options.B: Correct. $\text{NaOH}$ neutralises propanoic acid in a simple acid-alkali reaction to give sodium propanoate and water only, so no gas is produced.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ is a carbonate and reacts with propanoic acid to give sodium propanoate plus water and carbon dioxide gas, so gas would be seen.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4$ is a neutral salt, not a base or carbonate, so it will not react with a weak acid like propanoic acid to form sodium propanoate.
